header.userPrompt:
Warn at confirm when a bank statement's product type or currency differs from the same card's existing statements. Implements issue #123.

## Problem
Some statements (e.g. prepaid cards) get their product type misdetected during extraction — often read as "credit" when the card is really "debit". The detected type is accepted at confirm, so the statement is saved under the wrong type, and it also fragments the account (account identity is bank_name + product_type + account_last4 + currency), drifting from the same card's correctly-typed statements. The user does not notice at save time; the draft editor already lets them fix the type before confirming — they just need to be prompted.

## Goal
Surface a NON-BLOCKING warning at confirm when the statement looks like an existing card but a field disagrees:
- Type mismatch: the user already has statement(s) with the same (bank_name, account_last4) but a different product_type.
- Currency mismatch: same (bank_name, account_last4) but a different currency.

A warning (not a hard block) is required: same bank + last4 almost always means the same physical card, so a differing type is almost certainly a misread — but last4 can occasionally collide across cards and a card can legitimately be multi-currency, so the user must be able to accept and proceed.

## Design (reuse the existing confirm-warning mechanism — do NOT build a new modal)
`ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction` already computes `BankStatementConfirmChecks.periodWarnings ++ overlapWarning` and, when warnings are non-empty and `acceptWarnings` is false, returns them for the frontend to render with an accept checkbox. Add the new case(s) as additional `ConfirmWarning`s there.

- Detect SERVER-SIDE (the server has all the user's statements; the draft editor does not necessarily).
- Add a repository/DAO query for the user's statements with the same (user_id, bank_name, account_last4) but a differing product_type and/or currency — the complement of the existing `findOverlapping` (which matches the exact 4-field tuple including currency). Return enough to name the existing value(s).
- Emit a `ConfirmWarning` that names the existing value so it nudges toward fixing rather than clicking through, e.g. "You've saved this card (••••1234) as Debit before; this statement is Credit — if the type was misread, go back and change it." Same shape for a currency mismatch.
- These flow through the existing `acceptWarnings` gate; the frontend renders them with the existing warnings UI. No new endpoint, no new modal.

## Out of scope / must NOT do
- Do NOT auto-correct the detected type/currency to match the existing card. Silently overriding an extraction result violates the repo's "no silent defaults" rule (see docs/guide and CLAUDE.md) and would mask the opposite error. Only surface the conflict; let the user decide (and edit the draft's type/currency themselves if it was misread).
- Do not change the stored type/currency without the user editing it.
- No new persisted columns; this is a read-only check at confirm.

## Conventions (must follow)
- Follow docs/guide/ (architecture.md, backend.md, data-infra.md, testing.md, antipatterns.md, ci-checklist.md).
- All DB queries, read and write, include WHERE user_id = ?; every list query has ORDER BY.
- New Tapir endpoint definitions (if any) go in lib/api/shared/ — but this change should need NONE, since `ConfirmBankStatementDraft` already returns warnings.
- Use Chimney for case-class shape mapping where it applies.
- No external API calls in tests; use the existing testcontainers Postgres.
- Public repository: no PII anywhere in code, tests, comments, or the PR text (no real bank names, account numbers, filenames, merchant names, or amounts) — use neutral placeholders.
- The PR description must NOT contain any claude.ai session link.

## Tests
- A confirm whose (bank, last4) matches an existing statement with a different product_type returns the type-mismatch warning, and the confirm is blocked only until `acceptWarnings` is set.
- Same for a differing currency.
- An exact-tuple match (same type AND currency) does NOT trigger this warning (that is the existing overlap case).
- Accepting the warning confirms the statement, and the stored type/currency is exactly what the draft held (not silently changed).
- A statement for a genuinely new card (different last4 or different bank) triggers no mismatch warning.

## Acceptance criteria
- Confirming a statement whose (bank_name, account_last4) matches an existing statement with a different product_type or currency returns a warning that names the existing value, blocking confirm only until the user accepts.
- No change to stored type/currency without the user editing it.
- Existing confirm behaviour (period warnings, overlap warning, reconciliation gate) is unchanged.
- Full test suite passes.

resultJson.description:
Bank statements sometimes have their product type misdetected during extraction (e.g. a prepaid/debit card read as "credit"). Confirm accepts the detected value, so the statement is saved under the wrong type. That also splits the account, because account identity is (bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency), so the statement drifts away from the same card's correctly-typed statements. The draft editor already lets the user fix type and currency before confirming. They just need a prompt.

This epic adds a server-side, NON-BLOCKING check at confirm. If the user already has statements with the same (bank_name, account_last4) but a different product_type, or a different currency, the confirm returns a `ConfirmWarning` that names the existing value(s), e.g. "You've saved this card (••••1234) as debit before; this statement is credit — if the type was misread, go back and change it." These warnings go through the existing `acceptWarnings` gate in `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction`, next to the period and overlap warnings. The existing frontend warnings dialog renders them unchanged. There is no new endpoint, modal, or column.

Hard constraints: never auto-correct or alter the stored type/currency (that would break the "no silent defaults" rule). Once the user accepts, what gets saved is exactly what the draft held. Existing period/overlap/reconciliation behaviour must stay the same. Every new SQL query is scoped by user_id and has an ORDER BY. Tests and comments use only neutral placeholders (no real bank names, account numbers, merchants or amounts).

tasks.title: Add mismatch warning kinds, the same-card mismatch query, and the pure warning builder
tasks.description:
1) In lib/api/shared/.../bankstatements/ConfirmWarning.scala add `case object ProductTypeMismatch extends ConfirmWarningKind("ProductTypeMismatch")` and `case object CurrencyMismatch extends ConfirmWarningKind("CurrencyMismatch")`, and append both to `values`. ConfirmWarningSpec already iterates `values`, so the round-trip is covered.
2) In BankStatementDAO add `findSameCardMismatches(userId: UUID, metadata: BankStatement.Metadata)(implicit conn: Connection): List[BankStatement]`, the complement of `findOverlapping`. It selects `id, document_id, user_id, #$metadataColumns, created_at, updated_at FROM bank_statement WHERE user_id = ?::UUID AND bank_name = ? AND account_last4 = ? AND (product_type <> ? OR currency <> ?) ORDER BY period_start, id`, with no period filter, using the existing `parser`. Add a scaladoc. Add a matching `BankStatementRepository.findSameCardMismatches` wrapper using the same `Future { database.withConnection { ... } }` style as findOverlapping.
3) In server/.../validations/BankStatementConfirmChecks.scala add `def cardMismatchWarnings(metadata: BankStatement.Metadata, existing: List[BankStatement]): List[ConfirmWarning]`. It emits at most one ProductTypeMismatch warning, listing the distinct existing product types that differ from metadata.productType, and at most one CurrencyMismatch warning, listing the distinct existing currencies that differ. Each message names the existing value(s), the statement's value and the masked last4 (••••<last4>), and tells the user to go back and change it if it was misread. Example: s"You've saved this card (••••${l4}) as ${existing} before; this statement is ${current} — if the type was misread, go back and change it." Currency message has the same shape. Make the distinct ordering deterministic (keep first-seen order from the query).
Tests: BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec gets a "cardMismatchWarnings" block: Nil → Nil; type-only difference → only ProductTypeMismatch, and the message includes the existing type, the current type and the last4; currency-only → only CurrencyMismatch; both differ → both kinds; duplicates are listed once. BankStatementRepositorySpec gets a "findSameCardMismatches" block reusing the seed pattern from the findOverlapping tests: it matches a different product_type and a different currency regardless of period; it does NOT match an exact 4-field tuple; it does NOT match a different last4 or a different bank; it does NOT return another user's statements. Use neutral placeholders for new values. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementConfirmChecksSpec *BankStatementRepositorySpec *ConfirmWarningSpec"`.

tasks.title: Wire card-mismatch warnings into ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction with controller tests
tasks.description:
In ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.apply, after `overlapping <- bankStatementRepository.findOverlapping(userId, metadata)`, add `mismatches <- bankStatementRepository.findSameCardMismatches(userId, metadata)`. Append `BankStatementConfirmChecks.cardMismatchWarnings(metadata, mismatches)` to the warnings list, after the period and overlap warnings. Do not touch `create` or `requireMetadata`, and do not mutate metadata. Update the class scaladoc to mention the new warning.
Tests in server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementDraftControllerSpec.scala, next to the Overlap tests and using `seedReadyDraft` + `reconcilingPayload` (override metadata via `.copy`; prefer neutral placeholder values):
(a) Confirm a first statement. Confirm a second with the same bank+last4 but a different productType and a non-overlapping period (e.g. February) so no Overlap fires. With acceptWarnings=false the response has bankStatementId None, warnings.map(_.kind) == List(ProductTypeMismatch), and the message includes the existing type. The draft is still listed and only 1 statement exists.
(b) The same flow for a different currency → List(CurrencyMismatch).
(c) The same type and currency with a non-overlapping period → warnings empty and the statement is created (an exact tuple is not a mismatch).
(d) Accept the type-mismatch warning (acceptWarnings=true): the statement is created, the response carries the warning, and the stored statement (via client.getBankStatement / BankStatementRepository.find) has exactly the draft's productType and currency.
(e) A different last4, or a different bankName, with a different type → no warnings.
Existing Overlap/period tests must still pass unchanged, since they use an identical tuple. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementDraftControllerSpec"`, then `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

resultJson.brief:
Modules:
- lib/api/shared: shared API models. `net.wiringbits.api.models.bankstatements.ConfirmWarning` (file ConfirmWarning.scala) defines `sealed abstract class ConfirmWarningKind(val entryName: String)` with case objects Overlap, PeriodLength, PeriodOrder, FuturePeriod, plus `val values: Seq[ConfirmWarningKind]`, which drives the JSON Reads, so new kinds MUST be added to `values`. It also defines `case class ConfirmWarning(kind: ConfirmWarningKind, message: String)`. `BankStatementDraft.Confirm.Response(bankStatementId: Option[UUID], warnings: List[ConfirmWarning])` already carries warnings, so no endpoint change is needed. Test: lib/api/shared/src/test/.../ConfirmWarningSpec.scala iterates `values`.
- server: Play backend, layered controllers → actions → repositories (Anorm DAOs).
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.scala: `apply(draftId, userId, acceptWarnings, acceptUnverified): Future[BankStatementDraft.Confirm.Response]`. A for-comprehension loads the draft, then `requireReconciled` and `requireMetadata` (which returns `BankStatement.Metadata` with trimmed, non-empty values). It calls `bankStatementRepository.findOverlapping(userId, metadata)` and builds `warnings = BankStatementConfirmChecks.periodWarnings(...) ++ BankStatementConfirmChecks.overlapWarning(overlapping).toList`. If `warnings.nonEmpty && !acceptWarnings` it returns `Response(None, warnings)`; otherwise it calls `create(...)`, which stores the metadata as-is and returns `Response(Some(id), warnings)`.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/validations/BankStatementConfirmChecks.scala: pure object holding `periodWarnings(start, end, today): List[ConfirmWarning]` and `overlapWarning(overlapping: List[BankStatement]): Option[ConfirmWarning]`. Business conditionals belong here, not inline in actions (AP-BE-03 / RULE-BE-009).
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/BankStatementDAO.scala: `private val metadataColumns = "bank_name, product_type, currency, account_last4, period_start, period_end"`, `val parser: RowParser[BankStatement]`, and `findOverlapping(userId, metadata)(implicit conn): List[BankStatement]`, an exact 4-field match plus inclusive period overlap with `ORDER BY period_start, id`. SQL uses Anorm interpolation: `SQL"""... WHERE user_id = ${userId.toString}::UUID AND bank_name = ${metadata.bankName} ..."""` and `#$` for raw splices.
  - server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepository.scala: wrappers like `def findOverlapping(userId: UUID, metadata: BankStatement.Metadata): Future[List[BankStatement]] = Future { database.withConnection { implicit conn => BankStatementDAO.findOverlapping(userId, metadata) } }`.
  - server/.../repositories/models/BankStatement.scala: `BankStatement(id, documentId, userId, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd, createdAt, updatedAt)`, `BankStatement.Metadata(bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd)` (all Strings except the LocalDate periods), and `BankStatement.Create`.
- web: BankStatementTemplatePage.scala (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatements/) renders `resp.warnings` generically in a mui.Dialog (one DialogContentText per message) with Cancel and "Import anyway" (re-confirms with acceptWarnings=true). It never matches on kind, so new kinds need NO frontend change. Note: the dialog title is hardcoded as "This statement may be a duplicate". Leave it alone (out of scope), but it can be mentioned in the PR as a follow-up.

Non-obvious facts:
- product_type and currency are free-form strings in the DB. Extraction emits "credit"/"debit" (ProductType entryName), and the user can edit them in the draft. Compare exactly, as findOverlapping does. Do not normalise case or auto-correct.
- Account aliases (BankAccountAliasDAO, Key(bankName, productType, accountLast4, currency)) were just added. Do not touch them.
- Existing controller tests confirm two identical `reconcilingPayload`s to trigger Overlap. Because the tuple is identical, the new mismatch query returns nothing for them, so those tests stay green. New mismatch tests should use a non-overlapping period (e.g. February 2026, with the transaction date inside it) so that the Overlap warning (exact tuple only) and the period warnings don't interfere. Jan 1–31 and Feb 1–28 are both 26–35 days, so no PeriodLength warning. "today" comes from the injected Clock, so periods in early 2026 are not in the future.
- Controller spec helpers: `seedReadyDraft(userId, payload): UUID` inserts a ready draft directly; `createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator).futureValue.id`; inside `withApiClient { implicit client => ... }` the calls are `client.confirmBankStatementDraft(id, acceptWarnings = ..., acceptUnverified = ...)`, `client.listBankStatementDrafts`, `client.getBankStatements` and `client.getBankStatement`. `app.injector.instanceOf[BankStatementRepository].find(stmtId, userId)` returns a view with productType/currency.
- Repository spec (server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepositorySpec.scala, around line 964): the "findOverlapping / overlappingStatementIds" block shows `seed(userId, metadata)`, built on `createDocument(...)` + `createStatement(stmt, metadata, Nil)` inside `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, and `createUser()`. `sampleStatementMetadata` lives in server/src/test/scala/utils/RepositoryUtils.scala. Tests run against the testcontainers Postgres; no external calls.
- Tests use ScalaTest AnyWordSpec + `must` matchers. Subject strings are method names only (AP-TE-03). Existing fixtures contain a real bank name, but new test data must use neutral placeholders (e.g. "Test Bank", "0000"/"1234"-style digits) because the repo is public.

Conventions: every DB query on user-owned tables has `WHERE user_id = ?`, and every list query has an ORDER BY. Failures throw RuntimeException. Use Chimney for case-class mapping where 2+ fields are shared (not expected to be needed here). No new columns, migrations or endpoints. Never silently change type/currency. Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing. During a task, verify only with targeted `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, never the full suite. No claude.ai session links and no PII in the PR text.

findings.title: `CI=true sbt Test/compile` was killed (exit 137) before finishing

reason.text: Environmental, and the gate is still not met. dmesg confirms the global OOM killer killed the sbt java process. The host has 7.6 GiB of RAM, no swap and about 2.5 GiB available, because other sessions' JVMs run sbt builds concurrently (a second sbt was compiling another worktree at the same time). I re-ran it twice in the foreground, once with the repo's 4G heap and once with -J-Xmx2560m and a 1G metaspace cap; both runs were OOM-killed (exit 137). No code change can fix this, so I did not change the repo's .sbtopts, and I did not run the full suite or push. The changed modules compile: the targeted server and apiJVM testOnly runs compiled main and test sources and passed (90 + 3 tests). The web module, the only one the killed runs never finished compiling, has no changes in this task. Re-run `CI=true sbt Test/compile` once the host has free memory (no other sbt sessions running), and do not push until it exits 0.
